title: Malta Year 8 Math Chapter 9 — Sequences Practice
question: 30 sequence questions: 10 Easy, 10 Medium, 10 Hard.
intro:
**Three levels:**

- Easy: next term, the difference, missing terms
- Medium: the nth term gives any term; which term is it?
- Hard: find the rule, then use it; matchstick and tile patterns

- **Answers:** type the number.
- Use the ± button for a minus.

questions.title: Next term
questions.solution:
\[26 - 5 = \boxed{21}\]

It goes down by 5; \(31\) goes up.

questions.title: Next term
questions.solution:
\[1 + 3 = \boxed{4}\]

The step is \(+3\) all the way, also past zero.

questions.title: Next term, multiply
questions.solution:
\[24\times2 = \boxed{48}\]

The gaps grow (3, 6, 12), so it is \(\times2\), not \(+\) a fixed number.

questions.title: Next term, halve
questions.solution:
\[10\div2 = \boxed{5}\]

\(0\) takes 10 away; the rule is halve.

questions.title: The difference, going down
questions.prompt:
What is the difference of \(50, 46, 42, 38, \ldots\)?

Use the ± button for a minus.
questions.solution:
\[46 - 50 = \boxed{-4}\]

It goes down, so the difference is negative.

questions.title: Missing term
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} d &= 6 \\ 15 - 6 &= \boxed{9} \end{aligned}\]

Go back one step: take the difference away.

questions.title: Term from the rule
questions.prompt:
The nth term is \(4n + 1\).

Find the 10th term.

questions.title: Term from the rule
questions.prompt:
The nth term is \(5n - 2\).

Find the 6th term.

questions.title: Term from the rule
questions.prompt:
The nth term is \(2n + 9\).

Find the 20th term.

questions.title: Term from the rule
questions.prompt:
The nth term is \(7n - 4\).

Find the 1st term.

questions.title: Term from the rule
questions.prompt:
The nth term is \(30 - 2n\).

Find the 8th term.

questions.title: Term from the rule
questions.prompt:
The nth term is \(3n + 5\).

Find the 100th term.

questions.title: Which term?
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} 2n + 5 &= 45 \\ 2n &= 40 \\ n &= \boxed{20} \end{aligned}\]

\(25\) forgets to take the 5 off first.

questions.title: Find the rule
questions.prompt: Which is the nth term of \(5, 9, 13, 17, \ldots\)?
questions.solution:
- The difference is 4, so start with \(4n\).
- At \(n = 1\): \(4\); the first term is 5, and \(5 - 4 = 1\).

\[\boxed{4n + 1}\]

\(n + 4\) adds 1 each time; \(4n + 5\) starts at 9.

questions.title: Find the rule
questions.prompt: Which is the nth term of \(8, 11, 14, 17, \ldots\)?
questions.solution:
- The difference is 3, so start with \(3n\).
- At \(n = 1\): \(3\); the first term is 8, and \(8 - 3 = 5\).

\[\boxed{3n + 5}\]

\(3n + 8\) starts at 11: the 1st term must come out as 8.

questions.title: Find the rule
questions.prompt: Which is the nth term of \(2, 8, 14, 20, \ldots\)?
questions.solution:
- The difference is 6, so start with \(6n\).
- At \(n = 1\): \(6\); the first term is 2, and \(2 - 6 = -4\).

\[\boxed{6n - 4}\]

\(6n + 2\) starts at 8; take 4 away to start at 2.

questions.title: Rule, then a term
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} d &= 3 \\ 7 - 3 &= 4 \\ & 3n + 4 \\ 3\times20 + 4 &= \boxed{64} \end{aligned}\]

\(67\) uses \(3n + 7\): the start needs fixing.

questions.title: Matchsticks
questions.prompt:
Squares in a row use 4, 7, 10 matchsticks for patterns 1, 2, 3.

How many sticks does pattern 12 use?
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} & 3n + 1 \\ 3\times12 + 1 &= \boxed{37} \end{aligned}\]

\(40\) is \(10 + 3\times10\): count from pattern 1, not pattern 3.

questions.title: Triangles
questions.prompt:
Triangles in a row use 3, 5, 7 matchsticks for patterns 1, 2, 3.

How many sticks does pattern 15 use?
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} & 2n + 1 \\ 2\times15 + 1 &= \boxed{31} \end{aligned}\]

Each new triangle adds 2 sticks, so start with \(2n\).

questions.title: Tiles
questions.prompt:
A path of tiles uses 6, 10, 14 tiles for patterns 1, 2, 3.

Which pattern uses 50 tiles?

questions.title: Festa chairs
questions.prompt:
At a festa, row 1 has 12 chairs, row 2 has 15, row 3 has 18.

How many chairs are in row 10?

takeaway:
- Find the difference first.
- nth term: difference × n, then fix the start (first term − difference).
- Any term: put n into the rule. Which term: set the rule equal to the number and solve.
